changes.text:
# doc-linter

An agent-assisted documentation assessment tool. Writers express editorial guidance through examples, and deterministic and model-assisted checks contribute evidence-backed findings.

What it does today, in brief:

- **`assess`** examines the complete revised ordinary Markdown files of a GitHub.com pull request at one captured head commit.
  - It uses checks run by a pinned, verified Vale.
  - A **direct** check reports findings, with exact proposed corrections where the rule states one.
  - A **contextual** check collects candidates that a model judges only when you explicitly request one (`--judge-model`). Without a judge they stay unresolved.
- **`review`** runs the same assessment and serves a local page (this machine only). There you select findings, edit comment wording and export only the selected feedback as a local file. Posting to GitHub belongs to a separate review-mapping tool that is not integrated.
- **`examples`** runs each check's executable examples through the same implementation, so writer-maintained examples define and test a check's behavior.

Two demonstration checks ship: `spelling.recieve` (direct) and `phrasing.effort-minimizing` (contextual). Neither is adopted editorial policy.

Contracts and design: [first increment](docs/first-increment.md), [foundation design](docs/foundation-design.md), [judgment seam](docs/judgment-seam.md), [local review](docs/review-increment.md), [check authoring guide](docs/authoring-guide.md). Validation records are in [docs/validation/](docs/validation/).

Installation has been validated from a packed tarball and from a local Git source pinned to a commit, each into an empty directory. The private GitHub `npx` route has not been verified live yet.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22.12 or newer.
- The GitHub CLI (`gh`), authenticated for github.com (`gh auth login`). doc-linter reads through your `gh` and never changes its authentication.
- HTTPS access to GitHub release assets on first use. doc-linter downloads the pinned Vale 3.23.0 from its official release and verifies its SHA-256 digests before use. You do not need to install Vale separately.
  - The verified tool is cached under `DOC_LINTER_CACHE_DIR`, or else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/doc-linter`, or else the OS cache directory.
  - The cache holds only the tool, never results.
- Supported platforms: macOS and Linux on arm64 and x64. Other platforms fail with a clear message.

## Installing from Git source

doc-linter is a single leaf package contained in this repository (`private` in `package.json`). It is not published to the npm registry, and there is no registry publication pipeline. It is installed from a Git commit, and npm builds it from source during installation. The repository commits no `dist/`, and no manual build step is needed.

**Verified locally.** Installing from a `git+file://` URL pinned to a commit, into an empty directory, has been tested. After it, `--help`, `--version` and the shipped examples on the real pinned Vale all work, with no GitHub login ([record](docs/validation/source-install-validation.md)):

```sh
npm install "git+file:///path/to/doc-linter#<commit>"
./node_modules/.bin/doc-linter examples
```

**Pending live verification.** The private GitHub route has not yet been exercised against the real private repository, so treat this command as unverified:

```sh
npx --yes "github:mike-north/doc-linter#<commit>" examples
```

Prerequisites for a Git-source installation:

- **Node.js 22.12 or newer, with its bundled npm.** Verified with npm 11.18.
- **`git` on `PATH`.** npm clones the repository with it.
- **Read access to the repository for `git`,** for example an SSH key or an HTTPS credential helper. `gh auth login` alone is not claimed to be sufficient; whether it is depends on how Git credentials are configured, and this is not yet verified live.
- **Lifecycle scripts enabled.** Do not use `--ignore-scripts` or `ignore-scripts=true`. npm builds the package with its `prepare` script, temporarily installing the build-only dev dependencies (TypeScript) inside its own clone. The installed package needs only its runtime dependencies.
- **Network access.** You need access to the npm registry for dependencies and, on first use, to GitHub release assets for the pinned Vale.
- **`gh`.** An authenticated `gh` is needed only for `assess`. `examples` does not use GitHub.

A packed tarball (`npm pack`) contains the built output. It installs with `--ignore-scripts` and runs the same way.

## Usage

```sh
doc-linter assess https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>          # readable output
doc-linter assess https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number> --json   # structured result
doc-linter examples                                    # run the packaged check examples
doc-linter examples path/to/examples.yaml              # run specific example files
```

### Reviewing and selecting feedback

```sh
doc-linter review https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number> [--judge-model …] [--no-open]
```

`review` runs the same assessment as `assess`, then serves a small review page on this machine only (`127.0.0.1`, random port). The terminal prints a private URL, which is opened in your browser unless you give `--no-open`.

On the page you can:
- read each changed document with its findings highlighted;
- inspect acceptable and unresolved candidates, which cannot be selected;
- select findings, starting from none;
- edit the comment wording;
- export only the selected feedback as a JSON file.

The export keeps the original finding evidence unchanged and records your wording separately. It is a local handoff file, not a GitHub review. Posting feedback to GitHub belongs to a separate review-mapping tool that is not integrated yet.

The session lives only while the command runs. Nothing is saved automatically, so export before pressing Ctrl+C.

### Contextual judgment

Candidate checks use Vale for recognition, followed by a contextual model judgment ([the judgment seam](docs/judgment-seam.md)). One ships: [`phrasing.effort-minimizing`](checks/effort-minimizing-phrasing/README.md). Its guidance and examples are a proposed demonstration awaiting writer review, not adopted editorial policy, and its judgment quality on real pages has not been established.

- **Requesting a judge.** Request judgment explicitly with `--judge-model gpt-6-luna` or `--judge-model gpt-5.6-luna` on `assess`, `review` or `examples`. The effort is fixed at low. There is no default model, no fallback and no escalation, and an unknown model is a usage error (exit 2).
- **What the judge receives.** Each check and document gets one model call with the complete document, the check's written guidance and every candidate.
  - A confirmed candidate becomes a finding with a message and no automatic correction.
  - If the host reports a model different from the one requested, the judgment is rejected.
- **Model host.** The exactly pinned `@openai/codex` 0.157.1 is installed as a runtime dependency, even if you never request a judge. Its platform package takes about 330–390 MB unpacked on disk. It runs with:
  - no action tools, user configuration or personal instructions;
  - no telemetry;
  - a private per-run home that links only to your existing login.
- **Login prerequisite.** You need an existing **file-backed** Codex login (`codex login` with the default `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"`) or `CODEX_API_KEY`.
  - A keyring-only login is not supported.
  - Without a supported login, the judgment run fails with exit 3 and says so.
  - doc-linter never reads, copies, changes or switches your login.
- **Without `--judge-model`.** Candidates are reported as unresolved (exit 4 for `assess`), and candidate examples cannot pass. Direct checks such as `spelling.recieve` are unaffected.
- **Examples.** `doc-linter examples` with no files runs every packaged check's examples. Without `--judge-model` it therefore exits 1, because the candidate examples fail. To run only the direct spelling examples offline, name their file, for example `doc-linter examples node_modules/doc-linter/checks/spelling-recieve/examples.yaml`.

The assessment covers every changed `.md` or `.markdown` file in full, not only its changed lines. Each finding includes:

- the file, line and column;
- the rule and its message;
- the exact quoted source text;
- when the rule proposes one, an exact replacement. Replacements are never applied.

Every changed file is listed in coverage with one of these statuses:

- **examined**
- **deleted**
- **out of scope**: not documentation.
- **unsupported**: documentation in another format, such as MDX or Markdoc.
- **unavailable**

Reviewed content is treated as data. doc-linter never clones or executes the reviewed repository, and it ignores any Vale configuration there, in your working directory, or in your home directory.

It also ignores Vale control comments inside reviewed documents, such as `<!-- vale off -->`, `<!-- vale Style = NO -->` and `<!-- vale Style.Rule = NO -->`. A document cannot switch its own checks off, and there is no writer-suppression feature yet. The check run records where directives were neutralized.

File names do not affect checking: `README.MD` is checked like `readme.md`, and paths that differ only in letter case or Unicode form are checked separately.

### Exit codes (`assess`)

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Complete, no findings |
| 1 | Complete, findings present |
| 2 | Usage error (arguments, non-github.com URL, invalid examples file) |
| 3 | Execution failure (Node version, platform, `gh`/authentication, transport, pull request changed during reading, Vale failure, a requested judgment that failed or was rejected (including a missing Codex login), internal error) |
| 4 | Incomplete: some applicable content was not examined or resolved (for example MDX files, unreadable files, alerts that could not be placed exactly). Any findings are still reported. |
| 5 | No applicable documentation changed, so nothing was examined. This is not a clean result. |

If no check is available, both commands exit 3; running nothing is never a clean result.

`examples` exits with these codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | All examples pass |
| 1 | Any mismatch |
| 2 | Usage error, including an examples file with no examples |
| 3 | A check cannot run, or there are no example suites to run |

### Which rule does `examples` run?

`examples` always runs a check's examples against the rule built into the command you are running, never against a rule stored next to the examples file. Each report names the rule configuration and guidance revision it used, on its `Rule:` line.

- **An installed `doc-linter`** runs any examples file against its own packaged rule. Use this to see how a released rule behaves on your examples.
- **To test a rule you are editing**, run your checkout's own command, as described in the next section.

## Contributing a check or example

Each check lives in its own directory under `checks/`. For example, [`checks/spelling-recieve/`](checks/spelling-recieve/README.md) contains:

- `check.json`: the check's identity, its declared role (direct finding or candidate for judgment) and its scope;
- `vale/`: the Vale rule and its configuration, which own detection and the proposed replacement;
- `examples.yaml`: readable examples with the exact expected findings.

A candidate check, such as [`checks/effort-minimizing-phrasing/`](checks/effort-minimizing-phrasing/README.md), also has `guidance.md`, the written guidance its judge receives.

Agents helping a writer turn an editorial concern into a check follow [the check authoring guide](docs/authoring-guide.md).

From the root of your doc-linter checkout, after `npm install`:

1. Add or change examples first.
2. Then change the rule if needed.
3. Run the checkout's examples:

```sh
npm run test:examples                                               # every check in this checkout (candidate examples fail without a judge)
npm run test:examples -- checks/spelling-recieve/examples.yaml     # one direct examples file, offline
npm run test:examples -- checks/effort-minimizing-phrasing/examples.yaml --judge-model gpt-6-luna   # candidate examples; real model calls
```

The candidate command needs a supported Codex login (see "Contextual judgment"). It makes one model call per example that has candidates.

`npm run test:examples` rebuilds this checkout (`npm run build`) and runs its own command (`node dist/cli/bin.js examples`), so the rules in your working copy are the ones exercised. The report's `Rule:` line shows a path inside your checkout.

Do not use `npx doc-linter` here. The checkout does not install itself, so `npx` could run a different installed or downloaded package.

A wrong expectation fails with a mismatch that names the line, the quoted text, and the expected and actual values.

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm run check        # strict type checking, then the pre-1.0 version guard
npm run check:version # the version guard alone (see "Versioning")
npm test             # all offline tests: unit (fakes), vale (real pinned Vale), package (packed tarball), host (pinned Codex host, loopback only)
npm run test:unit    # no network, no Vale, no model host
npm run test:vale    # downloads and verifies the pinned Vale on first run
npm run test:package # packs and installs from a tarball and from a disposable Git source; runs against a fake gh and an empty HOME
npm run test:host    # the real pinned Codex host against loopback servers with synthetic credentials; never a real model or login
npm run test:examples # builds this checkout and runs its check examples (see "Contributing")
npm run rehearse:review # builds and serves a SYNTHETIC review page for browser inspection (docs/review-increment.md)
npm run build        # removes dist/ and recompiles (also run by npm's prepare lifecycle)
npm run catalog:generate  # maintainer-only: regenerate the pinned host's judgment model catalog (its digest is checked at runtime)
```

**Live model runs are never part of `npm test`.** They use your existing login:
- `npm run live:smoke` makes one trivial structured call.
- `npm run live:evaluate` runs the bounded predeclared evaluation of the shipped candidate check ([instructions](docs/live-evaluation.md)).

### Versioning

doc-linter stays within the 0.x range of [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/), so a 1.0.0 is never cut by accident.

`npm run check:version` (also part of `npm run check`) passes only when the `package.json` version is a valid, canonically written SemVer version with major version 0.
- **Accepted:** `0.0.0`, `0.1.0` or `0.99.99`, including pre-release and build metadata such as `0.2.0-rc.1+build.5`.
- **Rejected:** `1.0.0`, `1.0.0-beta.1`, `2.x`, and any malformed, prefixed (`v0.1.0`), missing or non-string version.
- **Tags:** with `--tag <tag>`, the tag must also be exactly `v` followed by that version.

The **Version guard** GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/version-guard.yml`, check name **Pre-1.0 version guard**) runs this check on every pull request and on every pushed branch. On a pushed `v*` tag it also runs the tag check. It is read-only and publishes nothing.

**Current limits:**
- The workflow reports a failing check, but it blocks merges only once branch protection or a ruleset requires that check. No such repository setting is configured yet.
- The guard checks versions and tags; it does not create them. There is no release or publication pipeline.
- Moving to 1.0 would be a deliberate change to this guard.

### Maintainer-only: re-pinning Vale

```sh
npm run vale:pin -- 3.23.0   # re-derive pinned digests from the official release assets
```

`vale:pin` runs `scripts/pin-vale.ts` directly as TypeScript. It needs a Node version that runs TypeScript without a flag.

- **Tested with Node 24.14.**
- **Not supported on Node 22.12–22.17**, the lower end of the review runtime's supported range, because those versions do not run TypeScript by default. Use Node 24 for this maintainer task.
- **The built `doc-linter` command** is plain JavaScript and has no such requirement.

warnings.title: A proposal is delivered by a later mechanism of its delivery list
warnings.message:
The group `readme-pointer` is delivered as `companion`. `groupedEdits` is `[native-batch, companion]`, set by the caller (`--grouped-edits`, `delivery.groupedEdits`), and the mechanisms listed before it are unavailable:

- `native-batch`: The edit of `README.md` line 5: Lines 5-5 of README.md cannot carry a native suggestion (file-not-in-diff).
remedies: To use an earlier mechanism, remove the obstacle the message names, then publish again.
To refuse rather than fall back, list only the mechanism you require.
